description: Building FMS Aqua, GreenFeed’s fish farm management system, as an outsourced project, including its warehouse integration, with Claude Code at the center of how I design, build, and review.
highlights: Building FMS Aqua, the management system for GreenFeed’s fish farms, as an outsourced project; in daily use across about 40 ponds since September 2026.
Built the warehouse integration and the reconciliation view that checks every warehouse issue against what each pond actually consumed.
Use Claude Code as the core of how I design, implement, and review features.

description: Built the Sales module of FMS, the company’s pig farm management system, in a 14-person team: everything from a weighed pig to an order, a price, and an e-invoice. Also built the background workers that sync orders from Odoo to Solomon, 1,000–2,000 transactions a day.
highlights: Built the Sales module of FMS, the system running 32 pig farms for about 1,000 users, in a 14-person team (3 on Sales).
Replaced Excel sheets and paper slips with one digital flow from order to e-invoice: unit prices pulled from SAP and weights read directly from the automatic scale software.
Calculated price and payment from each pig’s actual weight and issued around 130 e-invoices a day with no invoicing errors, sending final transactions back to SAP.
Synced stock and pig status with the inventory and pig-status modules in real time.
Built background workers that sync orders from Odoo to Solomon, 1,000–2,000 transactions a day.

description: Building e-commerce sites and Telegram bots for individual clients, end to end: backend, frontend, and deployment on a VPS with Docker. The largest so far is DBL Store.
highlights: DBL Store: an online store for game accounts with 800 users and 1,433 orders; Google sign-in, points top-up, and instant delivery.
Telegram bots that crunch data and run custom commands for individual clients.
Deliver end to end, from backend and frontend to deployment on a VPS with Docker.

description: Built APIs for the internal lending portal and service gateway across the whole loan lifecycle (applications, appraisal, approval, and disbursement), integrating banking systems, MoMo, and partner APIs for money transfers.
highlights: Built APIs for the service gateway and internal portal across the loan lifecycle: applications, appraisal, approval, and disbursement.
Developed the disbursement and money-transfer processes.
Integrated MoMo, banking systems, and partner APIs.

description: Built and maintained Transaction Counter, the system branches use for telecom contract transactions, across backend and frontend, then helped rebuild it on .NET 6 microservices in a 5-person team. Along the way I wrote shared libraries for logging, caching, and data access, and hardened the APIs against SQL injection and request flooding.
highlights: Transaction Counter (2-person team, backend and frontend): contract transactions for 70 branches, including new contracts, address changes, and internet plan changes.
Split the system into SOA modules and built the UI with jQuery and Kendo UI in a module pattern.

Moved business rules into stored procedures so they could change without a rebuild, and kept every query inside the DBA team’s 20-second timeout on telecom-scale data: filter before joining, no per-row functions in filters, and dedicated day, month, and year columns where they kept queries fast.
Raised bulk-insert capacity from about 10,000 to 140,000 rows per batch by passing XML lists straight into SQL Server stored procedures, a technique I later reused at VietCredit and GreenFeed.
Applied CSOC security rules: SQL injection prevention, role-aware error handling, and request rate limiting.
Wrote a shared helper library for queries, logging, rate limiting, HTTP calls, and exception handling.

Service Request Transaction (5-person team): helped rebuild it on .NET 6 microservices with Redis caching, logs shipped through Kafka to Kibana, and a React, TypeScript, and Redux Toolkit UI built from Figma designs.

description: Maintained the company’s ERP and outsourced projects, and built a scheduled service that collected bank and lottery data every day, with Redis caching, centralized logging on Elasticsearch and Kibana, and Telegram and email alerts for results and errors.
highlights: Maintained the company’s ERP system and outsourced projects.
Built a Quartz scheduled service that collected bank and lottery data every day.
Added Redis caching to cut database load, centralized logging on Elasticsearch and Kibana across projects, and JWT authentication.
Sent job results and errors through a Telegram bot and email.
